items.q: The specification states conservation of momentum for a closed system. What is a closed system?
items.correct: One in which no mass enters or leaves and no resultant force acts on it from outside the system
items.misconception: One in which the objects are all sealed inside a container, so that nothing can escape from it
items.why: The everyday sense of 'closed' is a shut box, so the condition is read as a physical enclosure rather than as a condition on mass and force. Ask instead whether anything outside the chosen objects is pushing on them or adding mass to them.
items.random_wrong: One in which nothing is moving, so that the total momentum of the system stays equal to zero

items.q: In a closed system the total momentum before an event equals the total momentum after it. What is this called?
items.why: Both equations begin with mass and are taught within days of each other, so the second quantity is mixed up. Check what the second quantity is: velocity gives momentum in kg m/s, acceleration gives force in newtons.

items.q: Two skaters stand at rest on ice and push each other apart. Which statement about their momentum is correct?
items.correct: They have equal and opposite momenta, so the total is still zero, as it was before the push
items.misconception: Both of the skaters are now moving, so the system has gained momentum from the push they gave
items.why: Motion is equated with momentum, and the direction of the two velocities is not taken into account. Before the push the total is zero, so the total afterwards is also zero: the two momenta are equal in size and opposite in direction.
items.random_wrong: Each skater simply keeps the momentum it began with, which was zero for both

items.q: A moving trolley collides with a stationary trolley and slows down, while the second trolley moves off. Which description is correct?
items.correct: The momentum lost by the first trolley equals the momentum gained by the second, so the total is unchanged
items.misconception: Some momentum was destroyed in the collision, which is why the first trolley slowed down
items.why: The car visibly stops and nothing else appears to move, so momentum seems to vanish rather than transfer. Identify the whole closed system first. Momentum is transferred to whatever exerted the force, even if that object is far too massive for its motion to be seen.
items.random_wrong: Each trolley keeps the momentum it began with, since momentum is a conserved quantity

items.q: Two trolleys of equal mass approach each other at the same speed. What is the total momentum?
items.correct: Zero, because they move in opposite directions, so their momenta have opposite signs and cancel.
items.misconception: The total is found by adding the two momenta as plain numbers, giving double the momentum of one trolley.
items.why: Momentum is introduced through a multiplication, so it is treated like mass or energy, a quantity with size but no direction. Choose one direction as positive and give any momentum in the other direction a negative sign before adding.
items.note: no MCQ covers this misconception, so no third distractor was authored for it; none invented

items.q: A moving trolley hits a stationary one and slows down. Has momentum been conserved?
items.correct: Yes. The momentum lost by the first trolley has been gained by the second, so the total is unchanged.
items.misconception: Conservation of momentum means every object keeps the momentum it started with.
items.why: The word 'conserved' suggests nothing changes anywhere, so it is applied to each object instead of to the system total. Conservation applies to the total for the closed system: add up all the momenta before and after and compare those totals.
items.note: no MCQ covers this misconception, so no third distractor was authored for it; none invented

items.q: Is momentum the same thing as kinetic energy?
items.correct: No. Momentum is m v; kinetic energy is a different quantity, calculated differently.
items.misconception: Momentum is the same quantity as kinetic energy: it is worked out with the energy formula ½ m v², so its equation is the energy equation.
items.why: Both quantities involve mass and speed and are met in the same topic, so the two formulae become blurred. Momentum uses velocity once, with no half and no square: p = m v, in kg m/s.
